title: Trace cohort variance scrapbook
content:
Purpose / quick summary:
This is a working scrapbook for the recent E2E trace cohort variance work. Goal: produce a small set of repeatable experiments and heuristics to explain wide P95/P99 spread across routes that nominally use the same model and hardware. This doc is intentionally informal — notes, partial graphs, trace excerpts, and hypotheses.

Why this matters now:
- Customer-facing SLO regressions surfaced in app telemetry even though aggregate p50 looked fine.
- P95 and P99 have been drifting upward for some traffic cohorts (chat-like short-turn interactions).
- Need reproducible slices and lightweight mitigations (routing, cache hinting, batching policy changes) before next deploy.

Sampling & instrumentation notes (how traces were collected):
- Time window: 2026-02-20 -> 2026-02-26 (week of high anomaly counts).
- Sample rate: adaptive trace-sampler with 50k requests sampled (1.2% of total). Sampler triggered on routes with observed tail > baseline.
- Enriched trace fields: route, model_variant, seq_len, batch_size_at_emit, kv_cache_hit, coldstart_flag, runtime_qos_tier, host_cpu_load.
- Important: some traces miss kv_cache_hit (legacy telemetry). Filtered those out for cohort stats below.

Cohort definitions used for analysis (canonical slices):
- short-chat-warm: seq_len <= 64, kv_cache_hit=true, batch_size_at_emit in [1,2]
- short-chat-cold: seq_len <= 64, kv_cache_hit=false, coldstart_flag=true
- long-generation: seq_len > 256, typical batch_size_at_emit >= 4
- batched-bulk: batch_size_at_emit >= 8, usually asynchronous path
- multi-turn-miss: seq_len variable, kv_cache_hit=false, turn_index > 2

Key quantile observations (end-to-end latencies, ms):
- short-chat-warm: p50=85ms, p95=210ms, p99=410ms (wide tail vs p50)
- short-chat-cold: p50=210ms, p95=520ms, p99=1200ms
- long-generation: p50=420ms, p95=760ms, p99=1600ms
- batched-bulk: p50=320ms, p95=480ms, p99=900ms
Note: numbers are aggregated across two clusters (us-west-2 and eu-west-1) and both RTX-6000 and A100 nodes. Later slice by region/hardware.

Per-stage breakdown (example: short-chat-warm typical trace median and tail behavior):
Stages observed (names as emitted by tracer): ingress -> tokenize -> model-encode -> kv-lookup -> kernel-exec -> emit-handoff -> egress-proxy
- ingress: median 1-3ms, tail < 10ms — negligible contributor.
- tokenize: median 2-5ms, p95 ~15ms. Occasional slow tokenization spikes when input includes long emojis/unicode (not common).
- model-encode: median 12ms, p95 40ms, p99 90ms — correlated with seq_len and batch packing.
- kv-lookup: median 4ms if hit, p95 180ms if miss (depends on redis cluster timeouts and cross-AZ hops).
- kernel-exec: median 40ms, p95 120ms, p99 320ms — large variance tied to cross-batch contention on the GPU (see below).
- emit-handoff: median 10ms, but p99 often >400ms when downstream async queue backs up (observed spikes during bursty traffic).
- egress-proxy: median 3ms, p99 20ms.

High-level trace phenotype discoveries:
1) KV cache misses dominate certain mid-tail traces: in short-chat-cold and multi-turn-miss cohorts, we see kv-lookup p95 > 300ms. Traces show repeated blocking waits for redis CALLS that sometimes include a 100–200ms retry/backoff.
2) Cross-batch interference: kernel-exec p99 correlated with host-level GPU memory pressure and context switching. Traces show concurrent jobs with large sequence lengths causing insertion of bigger kernels and preemption on multi-tenant nodes.
3) Emit-handoff backlog: asynchronous writer thread pools into downstream queue (egress / response-store). When queue grows, the per-request emit stage holds the token until enqueue success — this shifts tail into emit-handoff rather than kernel. Many p99s move between kernel-exec and emit-handoff across windows.
4) Coldstart amplification: cold starts not only increase model-encode but also cause extra egress/telemetry waits as init tasks serialize. Coldstart traces have many small waits before kernel start.

Representative trace excerpt (short-chat-cold) — fields and dense timeline (IDs redacted):
- trace_id: TRACE-20260224-AX9
- route: chat.quick
- model_variant: rwd-ggml-13b-q8
- seq_len: 42
- kv_cache_hit: false
- timeline (ms): ingress 2 | tokenize 4 | model-encode 60 | kv-lookup 480 | kernel-exec 90 | emit-handoff 18 | egress 4 => total 658ms
Notes: kv-lookup was the clear pinchpoint here; redis logs show 2 cross-AZ retries for that key.

Representative trace excerpt (short-chat-warm with kernel tail):
- trace_id: TRACE-20260222-CZ4
- route: chat.quick
- model_variant: rwd-ggml-13b-q8
- seq_len: 58
- kv_cache_hit: true
- timeline (ms): ingress 2 | tokenize 3 | model-encode 18 | kv-lookup 4 | kernel-exec 420 | emit-handoff 8 | egress 3 => total 458ms
Notes: kernel exec here is anomalously high. Host telemetry at time shows GPU mem use 78% and one large sibling job started 120ms before this request.

Hypotheses (ranked):
A. Redis cross-AZ lookups and occasional network blips amplify mid-tail — mitigate by local minibatch cache or prefetch for multi-turns.
B. Multi-tenant batching leads to kernel co-location overheads; scheduling small-long job separation or soft isolation could cut p99.
C. Emit-handoff queuing is reactive to downstream persistence service — we can make enqueuing best-effort and return response while flushing to downstream (with acks) to avoid holding request.
D. Coldstart serialization arises from init hooks (metrics/kv warmup) — lazily initialize non-critical subsystems or parallelize warmup.

Quick experiments to run (cheap, 48–72h turnaround):
1) Redis prefetch experiment: for multi-turn routes, prefetch next-turn keys at start-of-request for turn_index>1. Measure p95 for multi-turn-miss cohort. (Owner: Priya)
2) Soft isolation pilot: reserve one GPU card per host for short-chat routes during high qps windows (traffic tagging + local scheduler tweak). Run 12h pilot on us-west-2 and compare kernel-exec p99. (Owner: Diego)
3) Emit best-effort toggle: make emit queue enqueue async-without-wait for non-critical downstream (config flag). Observe change in per-route p99 and downstream error rates. Rollback if downstream ack loss > 0.1%. (Owner: Tom)
4) Coldstart parallel warmup: refactor agent init to parallelize telemetry boot (non-blocking) and run smoke tests. (Owner: Maya)

Metrics & dashboards to add (short list):
- KV lookup latency histogram split by AZ and by key-size (added tagging).
- Kernel-exec p99 waterfall per host with concurrent kernel count.
- Emit queue length time-series with per-route breakdown and drop rate.
- Coldstart frequency by pod and correlation with init-phase CPU spikes.

Immediate mitigations (safe toggles):
- Increase kv client socket timeout and retry backoff jitter to reduce synchronized retry storms (config change, low risk).
- Limit maximum concurrent large-seq jobs per host via admission control (config gate).
- On high emit queue length, short-circuit response to client with 202 + queued indicator (feature-flagged).

Open questions / unknowns to resolve:
- Are the kv misses due to eviction patterns at the redis layer? Need eviction logs and key TTL histograms.
- Does hardware generation significantly change kernel-exec tails? Need stereo comparison (A100 vs RTX-6000) with identical traffic patterns.
- How often are multi-tenant sibling jobs the root cause vs node-level OS preemption? Correlate with host-level dmesg / cgroup metrics.

Next steps & owners (concrete):
- Collect redis eviction and cross-AZ latency logs (Diego) — due 2026-03-14
- Stand up short pilot for soft isolation on 2 us-west-2 hosts (Priya + Diego) — due 2026-03-16
- Implement emit best-effort flag behind feature toggle and run canary (Tom) — due 2026-03-18
- Follow-up doc with quantitative pilot results and suggested default configs (Maya) — due 2026-03-21

Notes to self / scratch ideas:
- Consider micro-batching micro-scheduler: detect small short-chat bursts and coalesce into small ephemeral batches (<=2) aggressively to reduce kernel variance.
- Explore client-side hints: if client indicates low-latency preference, route to isolated pool; else send to cheaper multi-tenant pool.

If you have trace ids you want me to re-run in the trace-player, paste them below. I'll attach flamegraphs and kernel timelines for the next pass.

-- Maya
